title: Junta Jets Bomb NUG Special Regional Military Command Near Mon-Bago Border — First Direct Strike on an NUG Regional HQ
detail: Between 11 a.m. and noon on September 24, 2026, three Myanmar military jet fighters struck the National Unity Government's Special Regional Military Command headquarters near the border of Kyaikto Township (Mon State) and Shwegyin Township (Bago Region), while artillery shells were fired continuously from the nearby Thein Za Yat area. The command oversees five tactical commands, 15 battalions, and three People's Defence Force (Pa Ka Pha) columns operating across the Mon, Karen, and Dawei areas. Reports diverge on the toll: IMNA/Mon News Agency reported at least 4 PDF members killed and dozens wounded, while MoeMaKa cited local sources putting the toll at 5-6 dead, including CDM Sergeant Nay Win Aung and PDF members, with commander Aung San Shar and CDM Major Tin Lin Aung reportedly among the wounded. Continued artillery fire and reconnaissance drone monitoring after the strike prevented rescue operations. This is believed to be the first time a regional military command under the NUG has been directly targeted by an airstrike.

media.caption: IMNA report on the junta airstrike against the NUG Special Regional Military Command headquarters.

title: MNDAA Delegation Holds First Senior-Level Talks in Naypyidaw Since 2023 Offensive
detail: A Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) delegation held talks on September 24, 2026 with the junta's National Solidarity and Peace Negotiation Council (NSPNC) in Naypyidaw — the first senior-level MNDAA visit to the capital since the Three Brotherhood Alliance's October 2023 Operation 1027 offensive, and arriving nearly two months after the end of Min Aung Hlaing's 100-day peace initiative. Discussions covered union preservation, federalism-based governance, inclusive peace dialogue, and reopening border trade; the MNDAA delegation sought formal designation of its Kokang-area territory as a 'Special Region.'

media.caption: MoeMaKa report on the MNDAA delegation's talks with the junta's NSPNC in Naypyidaw.
